punchline: The disk drive makers that lost their lead weren't careless. They kept doing what their best customers asked, and those customers didn't want the small drive that was about to win.
thirty_sec: Seagate's engineers built a small 3.5-inch disk drive and showed it to the customers who bought their drives. The customers shrugged, because the small drive held less. Christensen found the same story across the industry, as drives shrank from one size to the next. The leaders listened closely and kept improving what customers asked for, while newcomers sold small drives to desktop and portable computer makers. The small drives improved until the old customers switched, too.
